title: text
description: A run of CHARACTERS to type, on the `keys` channel. The one keyboard message that carries characters rather than positions, because its source has no positions: a phone's on-screen keyboard (and any IME) produces text -- autocorrected, swiped, predicted, composed -- and never says which physical key was pressed. The host types it as-is, bypassing its own layout, with no modifier flags. Everything a soft keyboard does that is NOT a character goes as a key event on the same channel: the phone turns Backspace, Delete, Enter and Tab into keyDown/keyUp of the matching position, so this never carries a control character. Rides `keys` (ordered, reliable) because typed text must arrive exactly once and in order WITH those surrounding key events -- an autocorrection is 'two Backspaces, then text', and that only means something in order. Modifier chords around soft-keyboard text (Ctrl+letter) are not represented and are deferred (see catalog.json).

text.description: The characters to type, in order. 1 to 1024 code points, no control characters. A longer run is split by the sender; the bound keeps a hostile peer from handing the host an unbounded string.
